text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will hold talks with President Ion Iliescu before signing the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty in Timisoara today. French President Jacques Chirac has sent written congratulations to the Hungarian premier on the occasion of signing the basic treaty.
- President Arpad Goncz accompanied by Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and Foreign Ministry State Secretary Ferenc Somogyi today begins a week-long visit to Belgium and Luxembourg.

- The government heads of the five CEFTA countries agreed at a Friday summit in Jasna, Slovakia, on further liberalisation of trade in industrial products and a step-by-step reduction in Slovenian tariffs on agricultural goods.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar Friday agreed to develop and improve relations in the spirit of the bilateral basic treaty.
- Slovak President Michal Kovac attended the fifth Slovak- Hungarian regional fair and exhibition at Magyarnandor.
- Parliamentary parties will discuss the two years of the cabinet in a day of political debate on Wednesday.
- Heads of the opposition Democratic Forum, Young Democrats and Christian Democrats will discuss cooperation on Wednesday.
- Consumer prices went up 0.3 per cent in August, for a year-on-year increase of 22.9 per cent.
- Construction of the airport terminal Ferihegy 2/B will probably begin this year.
- The US company Tenneco Energy will pay $25 million to steelmaker Dunaferr for a majority stake in the energy producer Energiaszolgaltato Kft.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A report by the Hungarian Energy Office shows that it considers a 15.7 percent increase in gas prices and a 28.4 percent increase in electricity prices necessary. (Sat.)
- Free Democrat leader Ivan Peto gave an extensive interview with this paper. (Sat.)
- The European Investment Bank announced that it will increase investments in Eastern Europe by 50 percent to ATS 22 billion next year.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Foreign Ministry State Secretary Ferenc Somogyi said that the European Union has given a favourable assessment of the Hungarian reply to the EU questionnaire and the Brussels Commission has asked for supplementary information before the end of September.
- The fund manager Europool may establish the first Hungarian fund to invest in foreign shares next month if the Securities and Exchange Supervision gives its blessing.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The Finance Ministry will reduce the sales tax on coffee and precious metals and will do away with that on chocolate in the experiment to find out whether tax cuts affect trading on the black market.
- Eximbank is willing to offer favourable loans to Hungarian enterprises exporting to Bosnia-Hercegovina against a bank guarantee.
- Szegedi Paprika Rt, the major producer of the traditional Hungarian spice, is on the brink of bankruptcy.
- Foreigners may participate in the future trading of shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange from September 30.
